headline: State Minister Mir Shah Alam criticizes opposition for 'fake' religious politics
summary: The Local Government State Minister accused opposition leaders of using religion for votes while failing to attend religious festivals like Durga Puja.
details: State Minister for Local Government, Mir Shah Alam, has criticized opposition parties for engaging in 'cheap' and 'deceptive' politics centered around religion.
Speaking at a press briefing in his constituency on Friday, the minister claimed that opposition leaders previously used religious festivals to gain votes but were absent from such events this year.

He specifically mentioned that while opposition leaders once danced to the beats of drums during Durga Puja and merged fasting with puja to attract voters, they were not seen at any puja mandaps this time.

Mir Shah Alam stated that the public has realized the nature of this politics, alleging that opposition leaders deceived voters by promising 'heaven' to both Hindus and Muslims during previous elections.
The minister also claimed that leaders of parties who frequently speak about the July-August events and the 'July Charter' were absent from the festivities.

Responding to a comment by the Jamaat-e-Islami Secretary General regarding the government and opposition receiving 'biryani' and 'chocolate,' the minister noted that for the first time in history, an opposition party is receiving chocolates.
He contrasted this with 1996 and earlier periods when the BNP was in opposition and claimed they were not even given a place to sit, let alone chocolates.
caption:
From 'dancing at Puja mandaps' to 'promising heaven' for votes—State Minister Mir Shah Alam slams the opposition's religious politics.

State Minister for Local Government, Mir Shah Alam, has criticized opposition parties for engaging in 'cheap' and 'deceptive' politics centered around religion.

Speaking at a press briefing in his constituency on Friday, the minister claimed that opposition leaders previously used religious festivals to gain votes but were absent from such events this year.

He specifically mentioned that while opposition leaders once danced to the beats of drums during Durga Puja and merged fasting with puja to attract voters, they were not seen at any puja mandaps this time.

Mir Shah Alam stated that the public has realized the nature of this politics, alleging that opposition leaders deceived voters by promising 'heaven' to both Hindus and Muslims during previous elections.

The minister also claimed that leaders of parties who frequently speak about the July-August events and the 'July Charter' were absent from the festivities.

Responding to a comment by the Jamaat-e-Islami Secretary General regarding the government and opposition receiving 'biryani' and 'chocolate,' the minister noted that for the first time in history, an opposition party is receiving chocolates.

He contrasted this with 1996 and earlier periods when the BNP was in opposition and claimed they were not even given a place to sit, let alone chocolates.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV

headline_marked: 7,500 [[Bangladeshis held in Saudi prisons]], says State Minister
headline: 7,500 Bangladeshis held in Saudi prisons, says State Minister
summary: State Minister Shama Obaed Islam reveals the number of expatriates detained in Saudi Arabia and raises concerns over the execution of two nationals.
details: Around 7,500 Bangladeshi expatriates are currently held in prisons across various cities in Saudi Arabia on different charges, according to State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam.
The State Minister disclosed this information on Friday while speaking to reporters after the body of Shahed Ahmed, a Bangladeshi national killed in Saudi Arabia, was repatriated to Dhaka.
Shama Obaed Islam stated that Saudi authorities periodically provide lists of convicted Bangladeshis, but the government is still seeking details regarding the execution of two nationals.
Nazrul Islam and Sweety Akter were executed on October 14 over allegations of 'immoral acts' at a mosque in Makkah, but Bangladesh was not informed prior to the execution.
The Bangladesh Consulate in Jeddah has written to Saudi authorities and the Saudi ambassador in Dhaka to request copies of the verdicts to understand the full details of the case.
While acknowledging Saudi Arabia's right to enforce its own laws, the State Minister stressed that Bangladesh must be informed when its citizens face such severe punishments.
She also questioned the efforts of the previous Awami League government and the interim administration in handling the case, noting that the alleged incident occurred in 2023.
The government is also working to secure visa extensions for Bangladeshis stranded in West Asia due to conflict and exploring support for those who have lost their jobs.
caption:
7,500 Bangladeshis are currently imprisoned in Saudi Arabia, according to the State Minister for Foreign Affairs.

Around 7,500 Bangladeshi expatriates are currently held in prisons across various cities in Saudi Arabia on different charges, according to State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam.

The State Minister disclosed this information on Friday while speaking to reporters after the body of Shahed Ahmed, a Bangladeshi national killed in Saudi Arabia, was repatriated to Dhaka.

Shama Obaed Islam stated that Saudi authorities periodically provide lists of convicted Bangladeshis, but the government is still seeking details regarding the execution of two nationals.

Nazrul Islam and Sweety Akter were executed on October 14 over allegations of 'immoral acts' at a mosque in Makkah, but Bangladesh was not informed prior to the execution.

The Bangladesh Consulate in Jeddah has written to Saudi authorities and the Saudi ambassador in Dhaka to request copies of the verdicts to understand the full details of the case.

While acknowledging Saudi Arabia's right to enforce its own laws, the State Minister stressed that Bangladesh must be informed when its citizens face such severe punishments.

She also questioned the efforts of the previous Awami League government and the interim administration in handling the case, noting that the alleged incident occurred in 2023.

The government is also working to secure visa extensions for Bangladeshis stranded in West Asia due to conflict and exploring support for those who have lost their jobs.

Source: Prothom Alo, bdnews24.com
